intro: Budva rewards visitors with a compact walled old town, a long seafront promenade, and sandy beaches within a short walk. Its nightlife and summer festivals sit alongside quieter coastal villages nearby. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Budva has no metro or tram. Local buses are limited, so most visitors walk or take taxis.
Intercity buses leave from the bus station, about a 20-minute walk from the old town. Herceg Novi buses run about every 30 minutes for around €6.
Taxis cost around €5 for a ride within town. Use a metered taxi with a visible rate card, or book through MonteGO, which gives upfront fare estimates.
The currency is the euro (€), not USD. Prices in this guide are in euros as listed on Wikivoyage.
Driving is hard in summer: traffic is heavy and old-town parking is scarce and costly. Leave the car outside the centre.

Walking is easiest. The centre is about 2 km², and the promenade links the coast; the seaside line is quieter. Tourist boats run to nearby beaches and Sveti Nikola island, but they are not cheap, and there are no €1 water taxis.

oldtown.name: Budva Old Town
oldtown.price_text: Free to walk · museum tickets vary
oldtown.hours: Streets open all day · shops and museums roughly 09:00–20:00 in summer, check on the day
oldtown.tip: Walk the walled streets early or late to avoid the cruise-ship crowds.

stefan.name: Sveti Stefan
stefan.price_text: Islet is mainly a private resort · view from the road is free
stefan.hours: Islet access limited · check on the day
stefan.tip: Most visitors see it best from the viewpoint on the coast road, since the islet is mostly closed to the public.

stefanbeach.name: Sveti Stefan Beach
stefanbeach.price_text: Public beach areas free · sunbeds usually paid, roughly USD 10–25 per day (estimate)
stefanbeach.hours: Daytime, roughly 08:00–19:00 in summer · check on the day
stefanbeach.tip: Bring water shoes, since the pebbles and rocks can be hard on bare feet.

cruise.name: Bay of Kotor Cruise
cruise.price_text: ≈ USD 25–60 per person (estimate, varies by operator)
cruise.hours: Usually half-day or full-day departures from Kotor or Budva · check on the day
cruise.tip: Book a boat that stops at Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks for the best views.

kotor.name: Kotor Old Town
kotor.price_text: Entry to the old town is free · city walls and church fees vary (check on the day)
kotor.hours: Streets open all day · wall climb and churches roughly 08:00–19:00, check on the day
kotor.tip: Climb the city walls for views, but start early because the steps are steep and hot in summer.

cetinje.name: Cetinje Monastery
cetinje.price_text: Monastery entry usually free · small fee for museum (check on the day)
cetinje.hours: Roughly 08:00–18:00 · dress modestly, check on the day
cetinje.tip: Cover shoulders and knees, and keep your voice low inside the church.

fishmarket.name: Budva Fish Market
fishmarket.hours: Morning, roughly 07:00–13:00 · check on the day
fishmarket.tip: Go early to see the fresh catch and buy simple snacks from stalls near the harbour.

mogren.name: Mogren Beach
mogren.price_text: Public beach free · loungers usually paid (estimate)
mogren.hours: Daytime in summer · check on the day
mogren.tip: Walk the short rocky path from Old Town to reach this quieter cove.

promenade.name: Budva Riviera Promenade
promenade.tip: Walk the seafront at sunset when the cafés and bars along the water start to fill up.

viewpoint.name: Sveti Stefan Viewpoint
viewpoint.tip: Stop at the roadside lookout for the classic photo of the islet, then drive on.

lovcen.name: Lovćen National Park
lovcen.price_text: Park entry low or free · park road and museum fees vary (check on the day)
lovcen.hours: Roads open daily, check seasonal closures
lovcen.tip: Drive up for mountain views over the bay, and check that the road is open before you go.

nightlife.name: Old Town Nightlife Strip
nightlife.hours: Evenings, roughly 19:00–02:00 in summer · check on the day
nightlife.tip: Head to the bars near the old town walls after dinner, and pace drinks since the nights run late.

prut.name: Njeguški Pršut
prut.price_text: Tasting plates roughly USD 15–30 per person (estimate)
prut.hours: Daytime lunch hours, roughly 11:00–18:00 · check on the day
prut.tip: Try the smoked ham with local cheese and wine at a family konoba in the village.

stays.why: Walled-town streets, the harbour and most restaurants are a short walk away. Quiet at night, but it has steep, narrow lanes and no parking.
The main town beach, close to the centre and the promenade. Good for easy walks into town and for beach days.
A long sandy beach with many hotels and beach clubs. Best for beach-focused stays; it is a short taxi ride to the Old Town.
A quieter, small-bay area with rocky swimming spots and sea views. Good for a calm stay; expect taxi rides for nightlife.

food: Try fresh grilled fish and seafood platters at harbour restaurants in the Old Town and along the marina.
Order local black risotto (crni rižoto) or grilled squid where the menu lists it, and ask for the catch of the day.
Eat at the Old Town cafés in the morning and the seafront restaurants at sunset; prices are higher right by the walls.
Look for local bakeries and burek or pljeskavica stands for a cheap lunch away from the main promenade.
Check menus for euro prices and whether a service charge is included before you order.
more_time: Take a boat trip to Sveti Nikola island or a nearby beach. Tourist boats are not cheap, so compare prices at the marina first.
Spend a day in Herceg Novi. Intercity buses run about every 30 minutes for around €6 each way.
Visit Kotor or Perast for a historic day trip. Check bus or taxi times before you go, as schedules change by season.
